topics.label: Faithful reproduction
topics.rule: Code when the ad asserts, with an explicit accuracy qualifier (exact, faithful, true, actual, original, authentic, natural, perfect, flawless, 'down to the smallest detail'), that the instrument reproduces the real playing of the artists. A bare 'plays the great pianists' without such a qualifier does not count.

examples.quote: Getreue Wiedergabe des Spiels berühmter KLAVIER-Virtuosen
examples.gloss: Faithful reproduction of the playing of famous piano virtuosos

examples.quote: Every shade and degree of accent, rhythm, and tone is duplicated perfectly and exactly as the Artist rendered it—nothing is added, nothing lost.

topics.label: Touch, nuance and individuality
topics.rule: Code when the ad specifies what is preserved beyond the notes: touch, nuance/shading, dynamics, tempo, rhythm, phrasing, pedalling, tone colour, technique, or the pianist's individuality, personality or characteristic traits (incl. 'individual interpretation', each pianist being recognizable).

examples.quote: das Klavierspiel eines Künstlers mit all' seinen persönlichen Eigenschaften - des Anschlags, der Phrasierung, des Pedalgebrauchs etc. zu verewigen
examples.gloss: to immortalize an artist's piano playing with all its personal qualities – touch, phrasing, use of the pedal etc.

examples.quote: återgifver det karaktäristiska hos hvarje pianist, hans anslag, nyansering, tempo- och pedalbehandling
examples.gloss: reproduces what is characteristic of each pianist, his touch, nuancing, handling of tempo and pedal

topics.label: Illusion of the artist's presence
topics.rule: Code when the ad claims the reproduction creates the illusion that the artist is physically present, or is indistinguishable from live playing: 'as if the artist were seated at the piano', 'close your eyes', 'deceives even the artists', 'you can hardly tell the difference', 'living performances in your home'.

examples.quote: daß man wirklich meint, den betr. Künstler in Person vor sich zu haben und ihn spielen zu hören
examples.gloss: that one really believes one has the artist in person before one and hears him play

examples.quote: so vivid, so real, that it deceives even the great artists themselves

topics.label: Soul and life of the playing
topics.rule: Code when the ad claims that the artist's soul, spirit, feeling or inner life is captured or transmitted ('living soul of the artist', 'Musikseele', 'played his soul into the Welte', 'his spirit will pervade the room', 'what a great artist feels and thinks').

examples.quote: The Welte-Mignon Autograph Piano Is the Living Soul of the Artist
Die auswechselbare Notenrolle ist die Musikseele des Meisters.
examples.gloss: The exchangeable music roll is the musical soul of the master.

topics.label: Art, not mechanism
topics.rule: Code when the instrument is set apart from mere mechanism: it plays humanly/artistically, has genuine artistic value or significance, is 'not to be confused' with merely mechanical players, or has lost 'every trace of the mechanical'.

examples.quote: Das Reproduktionsklavier hat nichts gemein mit mechanischen Spielapparaten wie Pianola, Phonola etc.
examples.gloss: The reproducing piano has nothing in common with mechanical playing devices such as Pianola, Phonola etc.

examples.quote: Welte-Mignon spielt menschlich, deshalb künstlerisch.
examples.gloss: Welte-Mignon plays humanly, therefore artistically.

topics.label: The artist hears himself
topics.rule: Code when a performer hears his or her own recorded playing and testifies to recognizing it, or the ad narrates such a scene (Pugno 'I have heard myself', Grieg recognizing his own touch, Paderewski listening to his own playing).

examples.quote: Raoul Pugno: Es ist das erste Mal, dass ich mich selbst gehört habe. Ich habe mein Spiel genau wiedererkannt.
examples.gloss: Raoul Pugno: It is the first time that I have heard myself. I recognized my playing exactly.

examples.quote: the maestro instantly recognized his own touch

topics.label: Phantom hands and the self-playing piano
topics.rule: Code for imagery of ghostly or invisible performers: 'phantom fingers/hands', the slogan 'The Master's Fingers on your piano', keys moving with nobody seated, semi-transparent pianists or hands, or an illustrated piano playing with no one at it.

examples.quote: WATCH the keys of your piano moving, though no one sits before it!
These are the Phantom Hands of a thousand immortal pianists

topics.group: Time: immortality and the lost past
topics.label: Immortality and posterity
topics.rule: Code when the recordings are presented as preserving the artists' art beyond their lifetime or prime: immortality, posterity, future generations, 'lives forever', 'Instrument of the Immortals', art caught 'at the zenith', hearing artists who have died or retired.

examples.quote: das meine Kunst der Nachwelt überträgt
examples.gloss: which passes my art on to posterity

examples.quote: It perpetuates these performances so that future generations will enjoy the music of our present-day virtuosos when their personalities are but misty memories.

topics.group: Time: immortality and the lost past
topics.label: If only it had existed for Beethoven and Chopin
topics.rule: Code when the ad laments that the invention did not exist earlier, so that the masters of the past (Beethoven, Mozart, Chopin, Liszt, Rubinstein, Bülow …) could still be heard.

examples.quote: Man maa kun beklage at denne Opfindelse ikke allerede blev gjort tidligere; thi da kunde vi endnu den Dag i Dag høre Beethoven, Mozart og Chopin selv spille
examples.gloss: One can only regret that this invention was not made earlier; for then we could still today hear Beethoven, Mozart and Chopin play themselves

examples.quote: The regret of musicians must ever be that this great invention was not brought out in 1809 instead of 1909.

topics.label: Wonder, miracle and magic
topics.rule: Code when the instrument is called a wonder, miracle, marvel, magic or wizardry, or when the listener's astonishment or disbelief is stressed ('unbelievable', 'uncanny', 'struck dumb', 'how astonishing'). The routine adjective 'wonderful/marvellous' alone does not count.

examples.quote: Das Welte Mignon ist das Wunder der Wunder.
examples.gloss: The Welte-Mignon is the wonder of wonders.

examples.quote: It is modern magic.

topics.label: Epoch-making invention and progress
topics.rule: Code when the instrument is framed as a landmark invention or technical achievement: epoch-making, greatest/most remarkable invention of the age, a genius or sensational invention, 'admirable invention!', or the endpoint of a progress narrative ('after many inventions and many failures').

examples.quote: "Le Welte-Mignon" est incontestablement la plus grande invention du siècle.
examples.gloss: "The Welte-Mignon" is unquestionably the greatest invention of the century.

examples.quote: until the introduction of the Welte-Mignon it has never reached supreme perfection. But today the science has reached its apex

topics.label: Novelty, the latest thing
topics.rule: Code when the ad stresses novelty: 'New!', newest or latest models, just unpacked or landed, first showing, 'the last word', or that it is the only or first such instrument in the country.

examples.quote: Heden ontpakt: eene reproductions-Piano WELTE-MIGNON. Dit is het fraaiste, beste en nieuwste instrument
examples.gloss: Unpacked today: a Welte-Mignon reproducing piano. This is the finest, best and newest instrument

examples.quote: This last word in Player-Pianos

topics.label: The original and the first
topics.rule: Code when the ad claims that Welte (or the brand) is the original, the first or the pioneer: original invention, first reproducing piano ever made or sold, first pronounced perfect by the artists, holder of the original patents (in the body text, not only in a legal footnote).

examples.quote: The WELTE-MIGNON Is the Original REPRODUCING PIANO And Was the First Ever Sold in the World
Welte-Mignon ist eine Originalerfindung.
examples.gloss: Welte-Mignon is an original invention.

topics.label: How it works: technology and recording
topics.rule: Code when the ad explains or showcases how the instrument works: the recording process (photographic recording, the recording session), the electro-pneumatic mechanism, the roll as 'brain', electric drive from a light socket or instead of foot power, special features (full keyboard, fixed valves, expression patents), control devices such as the Musicalle. A product label like 'electric reproducing piano' alone does not count.

examples.quote: Der Mechanismus wird von einer Notenrolle, dem Gehirn des Apparates, gelenkt.
examples.gloss: The mechanism is guided by a music roll, the brain of the apparatus.

examples.quote: The original playing is recorded by a special Photographic process, which only the Welte possesses

topics.label: The name 'Mignon' is too modest
topics.rule: Code when the ad (usually via the Paderewski or Saint-Saëns testimonial) remarks that the modest name 'Mignon' falls short of the instrument's colossal effect or significance, or otherwise makes the name itself a sign of its importance.

examples.quote: Das einzige, was ich „Mignon“ vorzuwerfen habe, ist nur sein Name, weil er weder der gewaltigen Wirkung dieses Instrumentes, noch seiner kolossalen Be— deutung entspricht.
examples.gloss: The only thing I have to reproach 'Mignon' with is its name, because it matches neither the tremendous effect of this instrument nor its colossal significance.

examples.quote: et beskedent Navn for en beundringsværdig Ting
examples.gloss: a modest name for an admirable thing

topics.label: Superlative perfection
topics.rule: Code for absolute superlatives about the instrument or its maker: best, finest, most perfect, supreme, ultimate, incomparable, unsurpassed, unique, 'masterpiece', 'the perfect instrument'.

examples.quote: Welte Mignon, Verdens fineste Kunstspilapparat
examples.gloss: Welte Mignon, the world's finest art-playing apparatus

examples.quote: It has no peer. It is perfection.

topics.label: Superiority over rivals and exclusivity
topics.rule: Code when the ad positions Welte against competitors: comparison with or superiority over other player/reproducing instruments, brands or the phonograph; exclusivity claims ('only Welte-Mignon possesses the secret'); invitations to compare; warnings against cheap or unknown makes.

examples.quote: Only Welte-Mignon Licensee possesses the secret of perfect reproduction .
erkänna Mignonpianinot vara överlägset alla andra självspelande instrument
examples.gloss: acknowledge the Mignon piano to be superior to all other self-playing instruments

topics.label: Endorsement by famous musicians
topics.rule: Code for endorsement by famous musicians, conductors, critics, the music press or other celebrities: quoted testimonials, facsimile signatures, or statements that the great artists praise, recommend or choose the instrument.

examples.quote: Mignon ist für mich das unerreichte Ideal aller Musik-Instrumente
examples.gloss: For me Mignon is the unrivalled ideal of all musical instruments (Max Reger)

examples.quote: The Welte is without a doubt the most remarkable musical invention of our age.

topics.label: Satisfied owners and social proof
topics.rule: Code for social proof from ordinary owners and buyers: customer testimonials, 'that's why I bought it', numbers of instruments placed or families owning one, satisfied clientele, praise by laymen, adoption by many manufacturers presented as proof.

examples.quote: Das Welte-Mignon im Urteil seiner Besitzer
examples.gloss: The Welte-Mignon as judged by its owners

examples.quote: más de DIEZ MIL familias, que en esta República poseen estos pianos
examples.gloss: more than TEN THOUSAND families in this Republic own these pianos

topics.label: Royal and aristocratic patronage
topics.rule: Code for association with royalty and aristocracy: court warrants (Hoflieferant, fournisseur de la cour, hofleverancier), royal or princely owners and their testimonials, the Kaiser anecdote, imperial insignia, aristocratic mansions.

examples.quote: Ein Urteil des Grossherzogl. Badischen Hofes über Welte-Mignon-Pianos.
examples.gloss: A verdict of the Grand-Ducal Court of Baden on Welte-Mignon pianos.

examples.quote: the German Emperor ordered a WelteMignon Autograph Piano for his steam yacht

topics.label: World renown, awards and public success
topics.rule: Code for claims of international renown and public success: world-famous or known throughout the world, admiration or sensation in the musical world or abroad, triumphal tours, gold medals and exhibition awards, success at a public concert or exhibition. The bare epithet 'the famous Welte-Mignon' does not count.

examples.quote: ha sido premiada en todas las Exposiciones Internacionales con Medallas de Oro
examples.gloss: has been awarded gold medals at all international exhibitions

examples.quote: Van uit Amerika heeft de Estey-Welte reeds een triomftocht gemaakt door de geheele wereld.
examples.gloss: From America the Estey-Welte has already made a triumphal tour through the whole world.

topics.label: Heritage and standing of the firm
topics.rule: Code for the standing of the maker or the dealer: founding date, age, history and tradition ('Ye Olde Firme', 'Gegründet 1832'), size ('largest store in the country'), renown of the factory, financial strength.

examples.quote: Michael Welte, in 1832, founded the firm of M. Welte & Sons, a venerable institution
Største og førende Forretning i pneumat. Instrumenter. Etabl.1885.
examples.gloss: Largest and leading business in pneumatic instruments. Est. 1885.

topics.label: Reliability, quality and guarantee
topics.rule: Code for reliability and solid quality: proven in use, has worked perfectly for years, tested in every climate, durability, high-quality manufacture, guarantees, after-sales service and repairs, warnings that cheap instruments do not last.

examples.quote: Erprobt in jedem Klima.
examples.gloss: Tested in every climate.

examples.quote: Every Linconola is fully guaranteed—our reputation is behind every instrument sold.

topics.label: Hearing is believing
topics.rule: Code when hearing is presented as the proof: 'you have but to hear it', 'one must have heard the wonder to believe it', 'whoever has listened is convinced', 'hear it in comparison', a challenge to tell the reproduction from a live artist. A plain invitation to a demonstration is functional, not this topic.

examples.quote: Wer einmal dem WELTEMIGNON gelauscht hat, der ist überzeugt
examples.gloss: Whoever has once listened to the Welte-Mignon is convinced

examples.quote: You have but to hear it to realize that its playing is the artist's playing.

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: The great pianists in your home, at your command
topics.rule: Code when the ad promises the great pianists' playing in the buyer's own home and at the owner's command (whenever and as often as wished; 'summon', 'zitieren', 'at your beck and call'; the slogan 'The Master's Fingers on your piano'), or declares the instrument to be meant for the private home.

examples.quote: das Originalspiel der ersten Pianisten der Welt im eigenen Heim zu hören
examples.gloss: to hear the original playing of the world's foremost pianists in one's own home

examples.quote: Paderewski, De Pachmann, Hoffman and a host of others await your beck and call.

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Effortless: push-button, no skill needed
topics.rule: Code when the ad stresses effortlessness: push-button operation, no musical skill, preparation or personal effort required, plays without human help, makes entertaining simple, convenient enjoyment.

examples.quote: Ein Druck auf den Knopf genügt, um einen d'Albert, Busoni, Paderewski, Reisenauer etc. zu zitieren.
examples.gloss: One press of the button suffices to summon a d'Albert, Busoni, Paderewski, Reisenauer etc.

examples.quote: a person with no musical skill can have the actual playing of Paderewski

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Still a normal piano
topics.rule: Code when the ad reassures that the instrument remains a normal piano: invisible installation, unchanged appearance, can still be played by hand, several modes of playing, 'a two-fold pleasure'.

examples.quote: The Welte-Mignon* is invisible and does not interfere with manual playing.
Kan tillige benyttes som almindeligt Instrument.
examples.gloss: Can also be used as an ordinary instrument.

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Domestic comfort, leisure and intimacy
topics.rule: Code for scenes or promises of domestic leisure, comfort and intimacy: relaxing in an armchair, fireside and winter evenings, the family gathered, privacy and comfort of the home, holidays; includes illustrations of relaxed domestic listening (one to three people).

examples.quote: That delightful hour just after dinner—when the family is gathered around a cheery log fire
het genot de grootste pianisten in Uwen huiselijken kring te hooren spelen
examples.gloss: the pleasure of hearing the greatest pianists play in your domestic circle

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Entertaining guests
topics.rule: Code when the instrument serves social entertaining: guests, the hostess, dinners, dancing, house concerts, 'relieve the strain of hospitality'; includes illustrations of social gatherings (several people, often in evening dress) listening.

examples.quote: Ihre Gäste sind ganz entzückt wenn das WELTE-MIGNON ton- und klanggetreu das Meister-Spiel der ersten Klavierkünstler in Ihrem Heim erklingen läßt.
examples.gloss: Your guests are utterly delighted when the Welte-Mignon lets the master playing of the foremost piano artists sound in your home, true in tone and timbre.

examples.quote: the WELTE will interest your guests and relieve the strain of hospitality

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Culture, refinement and distinction
topics.rule: Code when ownership is framed as a mark of culture, refinement or social distinction ('vornehm', 'home of culture and refinement', 'visible token of culture', 'entertainment of the noblest kind', aristocratic mansions), or when illustrations place the instrument in elegant upper-class settings (evening dress, chandeliers, busts, period salons).

examples.quote: Uno de estos instrumentos en su hogar, es una representación evidente de su cultura musical.
examples.gloss: One of these instruments in your home is evident proof of your musical culture.

examples.quote: Die Instrumente des vornehmen Heims
examples.gloss: The instruments of the distinguished home

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Furniture and decorative design
topics.rule: Code when the instrument's appearance as furniture is promoted: elegant exterior, ornament of the salon, period models and case designs (Louis XVI, Georgian …), choice of woods, 'graceful lines'.

examples.quote: Elegant Ydre. En Pryd for enhver Salon.
examples.gloss: Elegant exterior. An ornament for every salon.

examples.quote: its graceful lines and artistic appearance will add charm and dignity to the finest home

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Women at the piano
topics.rule: Code when women are addressed or shown as the users, hostesses or focal figures of the instrument: the hostess, 'a woman and a piano', illustrations centred on a woman at or beside the instrument.

examples.quote: Una mujer y un piano no deben faltar en ninguna casa...
examples.gloss: A woman and a piano should be missing from no home...

examples.quote: A woman relaxes in the soft depths of her favorite chair

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Abundant and varied repertoire
topics.rule: Code for the abundance and range of the repertoire: libraries of hundreds or thousands of rolls or compositions, a hundred or more recording artists ('an army of artists'), variety across classics, popular music, dance, jazz and opera, 'every mood and occasion'.

examples.quote: a program to suit every mood and occasion
et Repertoire omfattende saavel alle Klassikerne indspillet af Verdens betydeligste Virtuoser, som Øjeblikkets kendte og populære Danse
examples.gloss: a repertoire comprising all the classics recorded by the world's most important virtuosos as well as the well-known popular dances of the moment

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Evocative musical imagery
topics.rule: Code for evocative word-pictures (or illustrations) of the music's emotional or scenic content: storms and Valkyries, gaucho dances, Venetian love songs, gardens of long ago, a twilight scene with the master at your piano.

examples.quote: Thunder of breaking waves; howl of the hurricane; crash of thunder
Le rythme précipité d’une mazurka, l’attrait d’un poème lyrique d’amour vénitien, le charme poignant d’une simple mélodie des plantations
examples.gloss: The headlong rhythm of a mazurka, the lure of a Venetian love lyric, the poignant charm of a simple plantation melody

topics.group: The masters at home: domestic life and taste
topics.label: Music for everyone: affordability
topics.rule: Code when the ad says the instrument, and with it great music, is within reach of ordinary people: affordability ('out of your reach—emphatically, no!', 'within everyone's means', 'at the price of an ordinary player piano', valued at £1150 but priced £575) or bringing art music to all homes and the widest circles. Plain price or bargain statements are functional.

examples.quote: if music is to be enjoyed by everyone, it must be within everyone's reach
vollendet künstlerische Musik in den weitesten Kreisen populär zu machen
examples.gloss: to make perfectly artistic music popular in the widest circles

topics.group: Beyond the home: education, other uses, identity
topics.label: Educational value
topics.rule: Code for educational value: use in conservatories and music schools, study by students and teachers, 'a college with 156 instructors', instructive listening, learning from the masters, self-knowledge for the pianist.

examples.quote: The Welte-Mignon can be likened to a college for teaching the art of playing the piano.
vom k. k. österreichischen Ministerium für Kultus und Unterricht zu pädagogischen Zwecken für das Wiener Konservatorium angekauft
examples.gloss: purchased by the Imperial-Royal Austrian Ministry of Culture and Education for pedagogical purposes for the Vienna Conservatory

topics.group: Beyond the home: education, other uses, identity
topics.label: Uses beyond private listening
topics.rule: Code when uses beyond domestic listening are promoted: concert halls, hospitals, sanatoria, clubs, restaurants, hotels, theatres, accompaniment of singers or violinists, ballet performances on stage.

examples.quote: För hem, konsertsalonger, musikinstitut, sjukhus, sanatorier, klubblokaler, förstkl. restauranger m. m. blir ”Mignon” en stor ackvisition.
examples.gloss: For homes, concert salons, music institutes, hospitals, sanatoria, club rooms, first-class restaurants etc. the 'Mignon' is a great acquisition.

examples.quote: Many recordings by notable accompanists afford competent support for singing at any time.

topics.group: Beyond the home: education, other uses, identity
topics.label: Composers playing their own works
topics.rule: Code when the ad stresses that composers themselves recorded or play their own works ('recorded by the composers themselves', 'played by the world's foremost composers', 'performed by its author').

examples.quote: låt oss spela en komposition av Sjögren eller Stenhammar, inspelade av kompositörerna själva
examples.gloss: let us play a composition by Sjögren or Stenhammar, recorded by the composers themselves

examples.quote: Klavérstykkerne er forespillet af Verdens første Componister
examples.gloss: The piano pieces have been played by the world's foremost composers

topics.group: Beyond the home: education, other uses, identity
topics.label: National and local pride
topics.rule: Code for appeals to national or local identity: domestic industry, national honour, local or national artists and composers, local customers or a local recording event, adaptation to the local climate.

examples.quote: ce piano qui fait honneur au nom canadien
examples.gloss: this piano which does honour to the Canadian name

examples.quote: dieses wundervolle Erzeugnis der heimischen Industrie
examples.gloss: this wonderful product of domestic industry

functional.label: Invitations to demonstrations, auditions, recitals and concerts (incl. free home trial)
Concert/recital programmes (pieces and the pianists 'playing' them)
Artist rosters (lists of recorded artists, portrait galleries)
Dealer name and address, sole agency / representation notices
Trade-in of the customer's old piano
Model names and product variants (Vorsetzer/cabinet player, Steinway-Welte, Quadrola, Musicalle, period models …)
Piano brands the action is built into, number of makes available, installation in the customer's piano
Catalogues, brochures and prospectuses on request
Cross-selling of the Welte Philharmonie organ
Trade notices (agents wanted, dealer franchise, warning against unauthorized agents)
